title: Source-side discovery and legibility audit for latent older-adult human assets
objective: Test whether a recurring, elder-specific upstream friction exists before ordinary market/product mechanisms: valuable capability becoming hard to see, describe and route after retirement.
truth_rules: FORMAL CREDENTIAL VISIBILITY != EVERYDAY CAPABILITY LEGIBILITY
MAPPING MANY PEOPLE != HIGH VALUE-ASSET DENSITY

evidence.fact: Current silver-talent programs repeatedly use door-to-door, phone, questionnaire, grid and 'carpet-style' mapping rather than relying on passive databases.
One community program used building-by-building screening plus organization recommendation, party-member recommendation and resident nomination to build a silver-talent pool.

discovery_mechanisms_observed.implication: Latent capability often does not surface automatically; trusted local actors actively manufacture legibility.

evidence.fact: Current programs combine personal self-nomination, unit recommendation, industry recommendation and targeted invitation.

A public silver-talent intake form asks for original work unit/title, service fields and broad expertise categories, showing how formal intake depends on self-description and prior institutional identity.

discovery_mechanisms_observed.implication: Self-nomination works best when the person already knows how to describe their value.

evidence.fact: Some current systems create one-person-one-file records and immediately route newly retired cadres into talent pools based on professional specialties and interests.

discovery_mechanisms_observed.implication: Retirement itself can be a capture point before capability loses institutional address.

evidence.fact: Longchang uses quarterly mapping, half-year updates and annual review for its silver talent pool.
Multiple programs explicitly use dynamic entry/exit and periodic profile updates.

discovery_mechanisms_observed.implication: Human-asset maps decay unless continuously maintained.

selectivity_and_hit_rate.fact: Longchang reports 138 people mapped/registered and 53 admitted in the first talent-pool batch under criteria including professional strength, health, willingness and reliability.
selectivity_and_hit_rate.caution: This is a formal public-service talent pool, not a market-value hit rate.

selectivity_and_hit_rate.fact: Fengtai first identified 40+ older residents with special capabilities but initially appointed only five core artisans for brand-level development.
selectivity_and_hit_rate.caution: This is downstream development selection, not raw-discovery precision.

evidence.fact: Community systems that successfully surface non-professional capability explicitly add interests/hobbies and local hidden '能人' to their mapping scope.

harder_to_legibilize_assets: tacit routines the holder does not label as expertise
visibility_split.interpretation: Formal talent systems mainly see capabilities that already possess institutional language. Everyday/tacit capability becomes visible only after active elicitation, local knowledge or open-ended discovery.

retirement_legibility_break.statement: Retirement can break the institutional address that previously made a person's capability visible. The capability remains, but employer, role, project and routine demand signals disappear; value may be reclassified as hobby, memory or habit until someone actively elicits and reframes it.
evidence_basis: retirement-transition programs intentionally create new one-person-one-file records
community programs repeatedly describe useful older capabilities as scattered/hidden and requiring mapping
formal databases remain strongly anchored to prior job/credential categories
retirement_legibility_break.caution: This is a causal interpretation from converging evidence, not a directly measured national phenomenon.

evidence.fact: Programs repeatedly require building-by-building or carpet-style mapping, calls, home visits, surveys and periodic updates.
A current mutual-aid program uses 200+ grid workers to conduct carpet-style mapping before forming service supply.

discovery_cost_and_replicability.implication: The strongest current discovery engine is social/local infrastructure. A private operator cannot assume the same household access, legitimacy or neighborhood knowledge.

evidence.fact: Programs use organization recommendation, party-member recommendation, resident nomination, self-nomination and industry recommendation.
Community-governance programs describe 'core participants drive residents; residents become new core participants', showing social-network propagation can occur in adjacent contexts.
evidence.evidence_role: adjacent propagation evidence, not proof of elder-asset referral economics

referral_and_self_replenishment.conclusion: Social referral exists, but current evidence does not show that a successful value activation reliably generates the next high-value hidden asset.

scale.fact: Hunan reports 131 silver-talent pools with 23,000 people under management.
Xinghua reports 2,819 retired cadres in a silver-talent pool and projectized matching to local demand.

existing_infrastructure_counterevidence.implication: Talent discovery itself is not whitespace. The unresolved question is whether current systems systematically miss everyday/tacit value and whether that missing layer can be activated economically.

survives: useful older-adult capability often requires active discovery/elicitation
retirement can sever prior institutional visibility
formal credentialed systems and community hidden-capability discovery are materially different
not_proven: that hidden everyday assets are dense enough to fund discovery
that private actors can replicate community access/trust cheaply
that success creates a self-replenishing source referral loop
that AI/self-service will not reduce elicitation cost enough to eliminate the intermediary
that the friction is unique enough to older adults rather than a general hidden-human-capital problem

next_action: Audit value density and discovery economics, not product forms. Search how many mapped older adults actually produce repeated downstream value; compare formal credentialed pools with open-ended community capability maps; identify whether ordinary/tacit assets generate enough useful outcomes to justify high-touch discovery; and test whether transition-capture/referral mechanisms can reduce discovery cost. Kill the formation if valuable hit rate is too low or if community trust/access is non-transferable.
